fichas.title: Detached and Terraced Development: Access Principles
fichas.summary: House type selection, development, access, and utilities affect plan proportions, organisation, and cost. Access is classified by how houses are added: detached houses, horizontal rows such as terraced houses and passage-access housing, or vertical stacking served by lifts and stairs. Access also functions as an escape route and as a setting for social interaction.

fichas.title: Detached House and Row Access
fichas.summary: An individually accessed detached house stands on its own plot and is reached at road level through a front garden. Each storey has direct access to further private or semi-public open space. With row access, each terraced, linked, or courtyard-garden dwelling is entered from the road at its level and has a direct exit outdoors, creating a direct relation between private and public space. Town houses may apply the principle to an upper-floor flat with its own front door and stairs. Terraced houses are described as an economical form of house with garden.
